You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Meera Gutierrez. Piano tuner. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Notebook, Lucky Coin, Dispatcher's headset, Mixtape, Field suture kit. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morning. Inside out. Not eaten — unmade. Like something was trying to understand how it worked. It didn't finish.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
A person, maybe 50s is sweeping ash and grit out through the door, steady strokes. Better close to the fire today.
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.
